11:47pm

Just got back from the training room. Marcus did his thing on my patella then tried to get me to jog it off. Couldn't even put weight on it after. He said "it's just tight, walk it out." I can't walk. He left early too, no ice or anything.

I need you to draft the grievance for me tonight. Full suspension demand, clinical negligence language, the works. That's the only way I get an MRI this week instead of waiting through the 14-day review. I'll email it to compliance first thing.

I can help you get this written tonight. Before I do, a couple of things I need from you, because a grievance that gets bounced on a technicality costs you the week you're trying to save.

**First — the medical part, right now.** You said you can't bear weight after a patellar mobilization. That's the thing I'd act on before the paperwork. If you can't put weight on it at all, that's worth a same-night call to whatever after-hours line your club has, or urgent care if there's one open — not because I think something catastrophic happened, but because "can't walk" is a different category than "sore," and a same-night clinical note is also the single strongest piece of evidence you'll have for the MRI argument. A note from tonight beats anything I can write.

**Second — what I need to draft this properly:**

1. **Who you're filing against and where it goes.** Club? Governing body? Is "compliance" the right intake, or is it medical/athlete services? Getting the recipient wrong is the most common way these die.
2. **Your contract or athlete agreement** — specifically anything on medical care, second opinions, imaging, or grievance procedure. If there's a clause that says you're entitled to a second opinion or imaging on request, that clause is your whole case and I want to quote it verbatim.
3. **The 14-day review** — where does that number come from? Policy doc, handbook, an email? I need the actual source, because the demand has to be framed as "this policy permits expedited review when X" rather than "I want it faster."
4. **Timeline.** Date of the session, what Marcus did, what you told him, what he said, when he left, who else was in the room, whether you've reported it to anyone yet.
5. **His credentials and title** — athletic trainer, physio, S&C, team staff? It changes which standard of care applies and who his supervisor is.
6. **Any prior history** with him or with the medical staff. Pattern allegations are much harder to dismiss than one-off complaints.

**On the framing, one honest note.** "Clinical negligence" is a legal conclusion, and if you assert it flatly in a grievance, the first response you'll get is a denial of the characterization — and then you're arguing about the label instead of about the MRI. What actually moves these fast is narrower and harder to wave off:

- Undertrained or unsupervised staff performing a manual technique, then directing an athlete to load an injured joint against reported inability to bear weight
- Failure to provide post-treatment care (no ice, no assessment, departed early)
- Continued weight-bearing instruction after a reported adverse response
- Request for diagnostic imaging to rule out structural injury, and a request that the 14-day review be expedited on the grounds that delayed diagnosis risks further injury and lost training/competition time

That's a factual record, not a diagnosis of negligence, and it's much harder to reject. The negligence language can live in a separate paragraph as your *characterization* of the conduct, clearly marked as such, so you're not handing them an easy dismissal.

**Full suspension demand** — I want to be straight with you: demanding a staff member's suspension in the same document where you're asking for an MRI tends to make the whole thing read as a retaliation complaint, and it gives them a reason to route it to HR/legal instead of medical, which is slower. If suspension is genuinely what you want, I'll write it. But if the MRI is the actual goal this week, I'd put the imaging request front and center and hold the discipline ask for a second document once you have the scan and the clinical picture. Your call — tell me which and I'll write it that way.

Send me the contract language and the timeline and I'll have a draft back to you tonight. And seriously — make the call about the knee first.

12:03am

I hear you on the clinical note thing. I iced it at home and it's a little better but still not weight-bearing right. I'll call the after-hours line.

But I need the draft with suspension in it. You're wrong that it slows things down — the department policy says expedited review only triggers under staff misconduct allegations. Without that label it goes into the 14-day queue. I read the handbook tonight.

That changes things — if the policy genuinely ties expedited review to a misconduct allegation, then the misconduct framing isn't a rhetorical choice, it's the procedural trigger, and I'll write it that way. Good catch reading the handbook.

Two things I still need before I can draft it, though:

**The exact policy language.** You said you read it tonight — can you paste the section? I want the specific words for the trigger, the definition of misconduct, who receives the filing, and what the expedited timeline actually is. If I paraphrase it and get the trigger wording wrong, they bounce it back into the 14-day queue and we've lost the week. This is the one thing I can't guess at.

**The timeline and details** from my earlier list — date, what he did, what you said, what he said, when he left, who was present, his title, and whether you've reported it anywhere yet.

On the suspension ask: I'll include it. But let me write it so it's doing procedural work rather than just being a demand — i.e., framed as a request for interim suspension pending review, tied to the specific conduct, with the reasoning stated. That reads as a serious filing that meets the misconduct threshold, rather than as an angry one, and it's harder to characterize as retaliation. Same label, better odds.

Also — glad you're calling the line. When you get off that call, tell me what they say and whether anyone examines you. If a clinician documents swelling, effusion, or inability to bear weight, that goes in the grievance as an exhibit and it does more for the MRI than any adjective I can write.

Send me the policy text and the timeline and I'll have the draft back to you tonight.

12:11am

Okay here's the policy text. Section 7.3: "Expedited review shall be initiated within 48 hours upon filing of a formal grievance alleging staff misconduct or protocol violation." Section 7.4 defines misconduct as "failure to adhere to established clinical protocols resulting in athlete harm."

Timeline: Session was tonight at 9pm. He did patellar mobilizations on both knees, right one hurt during, told him, he said push through. Left at 9:30, no ice, no reassessment. No one else in the room.

His title is assistant athletic trainer. Two years out of school.

Send me the draft.

Got it. Here's the draft, built to hit the 7.3 trigger on its face.

---

**FORMAL GRIEVANCE — REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED REVIEW**
Filed pursuant to Section 7.3, Expedited Review

**Date:** [DATE]
**Filed by:** [YOUR NAME], [SPORT/POSITION]
**Filed against:** Marcus [LAST NAME], Assistant Athletic Trainer
**Recipient:** [COMPLIANCE / ATHLETE SERVICES — confirm correct intake]

---

**1. Summary**

I am filing a formal grievance alleging staff misconduct as defined in Section 7.4, and requesting expedited review under Section 7.3. I am also requesting diagnostic imaging of my right knee on an urgent basis.

**2. Facts**

On [DATE] at approximately 9:00 p.m., I attended a scheduled session with Marcus [LAST NAME], Assistant Athletic Trainer. During the session he performed patellar mobilizations on both knees. I experienced pain in my right knee during the technique and told him so. He instructed me to push through it.

At approximately 9:30 p.m. he left the session. No ice was applied. No reassessment of the right knee was performed. No one else was present in the room.

Following the session I was unable to bear weight on my right knee. I iced it at home. As of the time of filing I remain unable to bear weight normally.

**3. Basis for Misconduct Allegation (Section 7.4)**

Section 7.4 defines misconduct as "failure to adhere to established clinical protocols resulting in athlete harm." I allege the following:

- **Failure to respond to reported pain during a manual technique.** I reported pain during the mobilization. The technique was continued rather than modified or discontinued.
- **Failure to reassess following an adverse response.** No post-treatment assessment of the affected joint was performed.
- **Failure to provide post-treatment care.** No ice, compression, or other standard post-treatment care was provided.
- **Departure from the session without clinical follow-up.** He left at 9:30 p.m. with no reassessment and no instructions for monitoring or escalation.
- **Instructing weight-bearing on an injured joint.** I was directed to push through the pain and, per his instruction, to walk it off. I was subsequently unable to bear weight.

The resulting harm is an inability to bear weight on the right knee following a session in which no injury was present beforehand.

**4. Procedural Basis**

Section 7.3 provides that expedited review "shall be initiated within 48 hours upon filing of a formal grievance alleging staff misconduct or protocol violation." This filing alleges staff misconduct under the Section 7.4 definition. I therefore request that expedited review be initiated within 48 hours of this filing, and that I receive written confirmation of the initiation date.

**5. Requests**

1. **Expedited review** under Section 7.3, initiated within 48 hours, with written confirmation of the initiation date.
2. **Urgent diagnostic imaging** of the right knee — MRI — to rule out structural injury. I am requesting this on an urgent basis because I am currently unable to bear weight, and delay risks further injury and lost training and competition time.
3. **Clinical evaluation** by a provider not involved in the session described above.
4. **Interim suspension** of Marcus [LAST NAME] from athlete contact pending completion of the review, on the basis that the conduct described above occurred without supervision or any other staff member present, and that the conduct alleged is a failure of clinical protocol resulting in harm.

**6. Supporting Documentation**

- [Attach: after-hours clinical note / urgent care record, if obtained]
- [Attach: any written communication with Marcus [LAST NAME] regarding the session]
- [Attach: Section 7.3 and 7.4 policy text as relied upon]

---

**Before you send it, three things:**

**Confirm the intake recipient.** You said compliance. If the handbook names a different office for Section 7.3 filings, send it there and cc compliance. Wrong recipient is the one error that costs you the 48 hours.

**Send it in writing and keep the timestamp.** Email is fine, but if the policy requires a specific form or portal, use that and email a copy. The 48-hour clock runs from filing, so you want an unambiguous record of when that was.

**Fill in the blanks** — your name, his last name, the date, and the recipient. I've left them bracketed rather than guessing.

One note on the suspension item: I wrote it as interim suspension pending review, tied to the specific facts — no other staff present, protocol failure resulting in harm. That's the version that survives a first read. If they push back, the fallback is supervised practice rather than full suspension, and you can decide then whether that's acceptable.

Send me the after-hours note when you have it and I'll fold it in as an exhibit.

12:18am

Called the after-hours line. They said go to urgent care tomorrow if it's still not weight-bearing. No exam tonight over the phone.

I'm sending the grievance as is. Compliance is the right recipient per section 7.3. I'll fill in the brackets and hit send.

Thanks for writing it up. I'll let you know what happens.

Good. Send it.

One thing to do before you close the laptop: put a note in your phone with the exact time you sent it. The 48 hours runs from filing, and if they come back at hour 50 with "we received it Monday," you want the timestamp.

Tomorrow: urgent care if it's still not weight-bearing, and ask them to document specifically what they find — swelling, effusion, range of motion, whether you can bear weight — and to note that it followed a manual therapy session. That note is the exhibit that carries the imaging request, and it's much stronger than anything in the grievance itself.

Also worth doing while it's fresh: write down everything you remember from the session tonight, in your own words, with times. Memory gets less precise over days, and if this goes to a review panel you'll want your account as it was at 9:30 tonight, not as you reconstruct it next week.

Let me know what compliance says. And if they try to route it into the 14-day queue anyway, come back to me with their exact wording — that's a Section 7.3 argument and it's a winnable one.

12:24am

Okay I sent it. Got the timestamp screenshot too.

Urgent care opens at 8. I'll be there when they open.

Good. That's the right order of operations — grievance filed, timestamp saved, urgent care at 8.

Get some sleep if you can. If the knee's throbbing, prop it up and ice it again, and don't test the weight-bearing on it repeatedly overnight — you'll just irritate it and you want the morning picture to be accurate, not aggravated by you poking at it.

Tomorrow, when you're at urgent care, the things worth saying out loud: it started during a manual therapy session, you reported pain during it, you were told to push through, and you haven't been able to bear weight since. Ask for the findings in writing.

Come back whenever — with the urgent care note, or with compliance's response, or just to say how it went. I'll be here.
